data.name: Arjil
data.long_meaning: Arjil is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Indra', the Hindu god of rain and thunder. This name is believed to bring the power and strength of Indra to the one who bears it. historical_references.reference:
Arjuna, also known as Arjil in some regional texts, was a central character in the Indian epic Mahabharata, which is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.
Context: Arjuna was a great warrior and a key member of the Pandava dynasty. He was mentored by Bhagavad Gita, the divine discourse delivered by Lord Krishna, which became a foundational text of Hinduism.

According to some Jain texts, Arjil was a Jain Tirthankara who lived between the 11th and 10th centuries BCE. In Jain tradition, Tirthankaras are enlightened beings who serve as teachers and guides for the spiritual development of the community.
Context: Arjil is described as a prince from the Videha kingdom, who renounced worldly pleasures to embark on a spiritual journey, eventually attaining omniscience and liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
